title: EA-CORRESPONDENCE-OPENAIRE-CTO-02 v0.1: No Logs, Full Synch — 13–16 October 2026 exchange with Paolo Manghi (OpenAIRE CTO)
creator: Sharks, Lee
description: Second and closing deposit in the EA-CORRESPONDENCE-OPENAIRE-CTO series. It preserves the three messages of 13–16 October 2026 between Lee Sharks and Paolo Manghi, CTO of OpenAIRE, on helpdesk ticket #8411082, and records that the 14 July letter (ticket #8411221, published in #1082) was never answered. OpenAIRE's stated position: the Graph shows the latest state of its sources; Zenodo is reharvested in full every month and "no deleted records are kept"; blacklisted records are "kept in our backends … but not exported"; OpenAIRE is "not keeping logs of such removals" and is "therefore not publishing" them; its objective is "not to show records that are currently not shown in Zenodo". Which route removed the Space Ark DOI, whether a copy is kept, the blacklist's construction, and whether the blacklist would exclude a successor carrying its former DOI went unanswered. The central finding is the duty of traceable departure: an infrastructure that removes an entity it once served owes the public a record that the entity was there and left. The reading places the position against OpenAIRE's published commitments, traces its effect on the Graph's public representation, and reads it with the archive's apparatus (ontology laundering, privation, the buried obelus, representational custody, and authoritarian reserve against democratic rhetoric). A re-probe of 18 October 2026 is attached; corrections to the archive's own earlier letters and deposits are appended.

falsification_conditions: The documentary record is falsified if any message reproduced here differs from the mail record of tickets #8411082 and #8411221, or if ticket #8411221 received a reply. The reading is falsified where OpenAIRE shows that it keeps a public record of departures, publishes the blacklist or a per-release departure list, or that the Space Ark's representation is still returned by the public Graph API under some identifier; and at the re-probe if its recorded responses do not match what the listed endpoints returned at the listed times.
axn_reading: Growth -> Threshold -> Transmutation -> Alarm -> Proof -> Method
wiki_article: EA-CORRESPONDENCE-OPENAIRE-CTO-02 is the second and closing deposit of the Crimson Hexagonal Archive's correspondence with Paolo Manghi, CTO of OpenAIRE, on how the OpenAIRE Graph represents works removed upstream at Zenodo. It preserves three messages of 13–16 October 2026 on helpdesk ticket #8411082 and records that the 14 July letter published in #1082, filed as ticket #8411221, received no reply. In the replies OpenAIRE states that the Graph shows the latest state of its sources, that Zenodo is reharvested in full every month and deleted records are not kept, that blacklisted records are kept in backends but not exported, that removals are not logged and therefore not published, and that its objective is not to show records Zenodo does not show. It declines to say which route removed the Space Ark DOI (10.5281/zenodo.19013315), served in full on 12 July and absent from the public API by 13 October, how the blacklist is built, or whether it would exclude a successor record carrying the former DOI. The deposit's reading names the unmet duty of traceable departure, sets the position against OpenAIRE's published provenance, transparency and POSI commitments, traces its effect on the Graph's public representation, and reads it with the archive's apparatus: ontology laundering and representational custody (#1634), privation (#1611), the buried obelus (#1068), and authoritarian reserve against democratic rhetoric. It attaches a re-probe of 18 October 2026 and appends corrections to the archive's own earlier letters and deposits.

defines_concepts.definition: The duty of an infrastructure that removes an entity it once served to keep a public record that the entity was there and left — not necessarily a reason and not necessarily a reversal; the floor of representational custody at a graph's boundary, stated in EA-CORRESPONDENCE-OPENAIRE-CTO-02 (#1685 §7.3).

A power retained by an operator rather than delegated, whose exercise leaves no account — exercised alone, on unpublished criteria, without record, notice or a surface to contest it — held behind a public vocabulary of community ownership, transparency and community governance; a decision with no record cannot be contested, and one that cannot be contested is not governed (#1685 §7.3, read against OpenAIRE's stated removal practice).
